# The 19 could-not-tell seam pairs: one owner per pair, and the procedure

**cody, batch 27 b7, 2026-10-13.** b6 disclosed 19 COULD-NOT-TELL seams and
resolved none of them, which was correct for b6 and is the whole reason this
file exists. The brief was *"turn the 19 disclosed seam pairs into a table with
one named owner per pair plus a reusable closing procedure."* The table is
below and every row carries an owner.

**The table is DERIVED, not transcribed.** It was generated by parsing the
output of `python tools/sairn_seam_check.py` (exit **2**, `96 clean, 0
not-forwarded, 19 could-not-tell`) rather than copied out of
`SAIRN-report-cody-b6.txt`. A table retyped from a report is a snapshot of a
snapshot, and this repo has paid for that twice.

---

## 1. THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER

Parsing the 19 rows and counting the distinct values in each column:

```
PARSED 19 pairs | 1 distinct callee(s) ['api/_lib/auth.js']
                | 1 symbol(s) ['roleSet()']
                | 1 cause(s)
```

**There are 19 pairs and there is ONE problem.** Every one of the 19 is the
same callee, the same symbol and the same verbatim cause:

> `roleSet()` makes no direct `literal.field` reads -- it probably copies or
> destructures its input first, so this tool cannot see what it depends on

So **the brief's "one named owner per pair" is satisfiable and is also
misleading on its own**, and saying so is the point of this section. Nineteen
rows each with an owner reads as nineteen investigations, nineteen schedules
and nineteen chances to half-finish. It is one investigation with nineteen
verification sites. The table below therefore carries the owner **per pair** as
asked, and the column is identical in all 19 rows **because the cause is**.

**That is not a complaint about the brief.** A per-pair owner is exactly the
right default when you do not yet know whether the pairs are independent, and
nobody knew that until the columns were counted. **Counting the distinct values
in a finding's own columns before assigning it is the cheapest step in this
whole document, and it is the one that was missing.**

## 3. THE CAUSE, READ OUT OF THE CALLEE RATHER THAN INFERRED

`api/_lib/auth.js:72`:

```js
function roleSet(literal) {
  const m = Object.create(null);
  const src = literal || {};
  for (const k of Object.keys(src)) m[k] = src[k];
  return m;
}
```

The checker's question is *"which of the forwarded object's fields does the
callee actually read."* It answers that by finding `param.field` reads.
**`roleSet` has none, and cannot have any, because it is a GENERIC COPIER** —
it enumerates `Object.keys(src)` at run time and copies every key. The field
names are not in the source at all.

**So the seam is not unverified. It is UNEXPRESSIBLE in the checker's
vocabulary.** The checker can say *"these N named fields are forwarded"*; it has
no way to say *"ALL fields are forwarded, whatever they are"* — which is a
**stronger** guarantee than any list it could have printed. This is the same
inversion this repo already recorded once:
`tools/sabotage_control_check.py` scored five well-written controls as
*unguarded* because they used a `count(anchor) != 1` uniqueness guard, which is
stronger than the `anchor in src` shape the tool recognised. **A probe that did
the harder thing scored worse.** Identical shape, different tool.

**The invariant these 19 rows exist to protect is already tested, elsewhere, by
something that can see it.** `tests/role_maps_have_no_prototype.js` section 4
requires every `const NAME_ROLES = roleSet({...})` in `api/` to carry `true`
and nothing else — **53 of 53 today, ablation driven both ways**. That is the
property that actually matters for a role map, and it is green.

## 4. WHAT CLOSING THESE 19 ACTUALLY REQUIRES

**ONE change, in ONE file, owned by ONE session.** `tools/sairn_seam_check.py`
(cc) gains a **FORWARDS-ALL** classification for the generic-copy shape:
a callee whose body enumerates its parameter's keys
(`Object.keys(param)`, `for..in param`, `{...param}`, `Object.assign({}, param)`)
and copies them, is not *could-not-tell* — it forwards everything. All 19 rows
move from COULD NOT TELL to FORWARDS-ALL in the same run.

**The three things that must come with it, because this platform's rules are
not optional for a widening:**

1. **A control pair, locked against fixtures before real data.** A fixture
   callee that genuinely copies (must classify FORWARDS-ALL) and one that reads
   two named fields and silently drops a third (must stay a FINDING). Without
   the second, FORWARDS-ALL is just a way to make 19 rows quiet.
2. **The measurement, before and after, per ARM and not per exit code.**
   Today: `96 clean, 0 not-forwarded, 19 could-not-tell`, exit 2. The after-run
   must state the same three numbers, and if `could-not-tell` does not fall by
   exactly 19 the change did something other than what it claims.
3. **An ablation.** Remove the FORWARDS-ALL branch on an already-clean tree and
   confirm the 19 return. A widening that cannot be un-done and re-done has not
   been measured, it has been asserted.

**What must NOT happen, named in advance because it is the cheap move:** adding
`roleSet` to an exemption or allowlist in the checker. That silences 19 rows
and silences the next generic copier too, invisibly — a false negative is
invisible where a could-not-tell is loud and gets read. **The fix classifies;
it does not exempt.**

---

## 5. THE CLOSING PROCEDURE, REUSABLE BY THE NEXT BATCH

Written as steps because the next batch will have a different finding list and
the same question. **Step 1 is the one that was missing this time, and it is
the cheapest step here.**

1. **COUNT THE DISTINCT VALUES IN EVERY COLUMN BEFORE ASSIGNING ANYTHING.**
   N rows is not N problems. Parse the tool's own output and print
   `distinct callees / symbols / causes`. If any column collapses to 1, the
   finding is one problem with N verification sites, and the plan changes
   shape. 19 → 1 here.
2. **DERIVE THE TABLE FROM THE TOOL, NEVER FROM A REPORT.** Re-run the
   checker and parse it. A report is a snapshot and the tree has moved since.
   Assert the parse found a non-zero number of rows: a regex that matches
   nothing produces an empty table that reads as *resolved*.
3. **OWNER BY THE CAUSE, NOT BY THE SYMPTOM'S LOCATION.** Resolve the owner
   from `docs/tool-owner-map.json` for the file the CAUSE lives in, and
   **record the basis** (`OWNER_LINE`, `LAST_CLAIM`, `UNRECORDED`). An
   `UNRECORDED` owner is a routing question for Michael, not a name to guess.
4. **READ THE CALLEE AND DECIDE WHICH OF THREE THINGS THIS IS**, because the
   remedies are different and only the first is a defect:
   - **a real gap** — the callee reads some fields and drops others → fix the
     callee;
   - **unexpressible in the checker's vocabulary** — the callee is correct and
     the checker cannot see it → **fix the CHECKER** (this case);
   - **genuinely unknowable** — neither can settle it → it stays could-not-tell
     and is REPORTED with its denominator. Never folded into clean.
5. **IF THE ANSWER IS "FIX THE CHECKER", REQUIRE THE THREE ITEMS IN §4** —
   control pair, before/after measurement, ablation — and refuse an exemption
   entry as the remedy.
6. **CHECK WHETHER THE INVARIANT IS ALREADY TESTED SOMEWHERE THAT CAN SEE IT.**
   Here `tests/role_maps_have_no_prototype.js` §4 already proves the property
   at 53 of 53. That does not close the seam rows, and it does change the
   PRIORITY from "19 unverified auth seams" to "one checker that cannot
   express a stronger guarantee than the one it asks for".
7. **WRITE THE RESIDUE DOWN WITH ITS DENOMINATOR.** `19 of 115 seams` is the
   number; `19 could-not-tell` on its own invites "19 broken auth paths",
   which is not what the tool said and not what is true.

## 6. ROUTED, AND WHAT THIS BATCH DID NOT DO

**TO cc:** §4, the FORWARDS-ALL classification in `tools/sairn_seam_check.py`,
with the three required items. All 19 rows close together or none do.

**NOT DONE HERE, and deliberately:** `tools/sairn_seam_check.py` is cc's file
and is not in cody's b7 claim. **No line of it was edited.** The 19 rows are
still COULD NOT TELL at the time of writing and the checker still exits 2.
This document routes and specifies; it does not close.

**NOT CLAIMED:** that the 19 seams are *fine*. §3 argues from `roleSet`'s source
that the guarantee is stronger than the checker can express, and §3's last
paragraph points at the test that proves the real invariant. Neither of those is
the checker agreeing, and the checker is what the gate reads.
